plates.side_label: 1920 STAUDINGER 'ÜBER POLYMERISATION': COVALENT MACROMOLECULE CHAINS (10,000–100,000+ UNITS) VS <5,000 DA CLUMP MYTH

plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked polymer-chain vs colloidal-clump comparison diagram from Hermann Staudinger (1920, Berichte der deutschen chemischen Gesellschaft 53: 1073–1085) contrasts the old micelle/aggregate myth (<5,000 Da rings) against Staudinger's covalent macromolecule chains (10,000 to >100,000 repeating monomer units remaining giant chains even after hydrogenation).

teach_overlay.detail: Inked polymer-chain vs colloidal-clump comparison diagram on period paper from Hermann Staudinger (1920, Berichte der deutschen chemischen Gesellschaft 53: 1073–1085) contrasting the old micelle/aggregate myth (<5,000 Da rings) against Staudinger's covalent macromolecule chains (10,000 to >100,000 repeating monomer units remaining giant chains even after hydrogenation)
teach_overlay.scale: chemists in nineteen twenty insisted no single molecule could hold more than a few hundred atoms — yet Hermann Staudinger proved a single strand of rubber or plastic is a continuous chain of hundreds of thousands of atoms bolted together
